identify.title: You pay two systems to hold the same number. Neither one is checking.

one.statement: Your 3PL quietly dropped the count by one after a cycle count.
one.body: You asked how a bright orange box that weighs five pounds disappears. They said “products can occasionally be misplaced due to an operational move on the warehouse floor.”

two.statement: Then they told you 2–5% shrinkage is industry standard.
two.body: Standard for them. Out of your margin.

three.statement: Black Friday. Your top product oversold by 30 units.
three.body: You spent the weekend calling customers to cancel. Lost the sales and the reputation in the same 48 hours.

four.statement: Year-end count: you got the total that’s missing.
four.body: Not which product. Not when. Not who.

identify.closer: You find out when an order can’t ship.

logic.title: Two numbers, side by side, every day

one.title: Both counts, daily
one.body: Every day, every product: what your 3PL says, what Shopify says, and the difference — in units and in dollars.

two.title: You hear it first
two.body: The moment it drifts past what you’ll accept, you know. Not the customer. You.

three.title: A claim, not a complaint
three.body: And you have the history: which product, when, how much. That’s not a complaint anymore. That’s a claim.

logic.footer: It reads both systems and writes to neither. Read-only, nothing else — the only thing it changes is what you know.

objections.title: The three reasons not to believe this — answered

one.a: Their shelf against their system. Nobody checks their system against yours. That’s the gap, and it’s where “industry standard” lives.

two.a: Ones and twos across 300 products, at your cost, every month. A 3PL owner said it himself: should be under half a percent. You can’t hold them to that without your own count.

three.q: “I’ll find out at the physical count.”
three.a: You’ll find the total. By then it’s a write-off, not a claim.

confess.title: “Products can occasionally be misplaced.”
confess.sub: The 3PL’s own words. Occasionally. For years. Out of your money.

solution.title: Your stock, accounted for.
solution.sub: No oversells at peak. Shrinkage you can claim back. A count you can trust your cash to.
solution.withoutBody: You find out from a customer. Or at year-end, as a write-off. And the 3PL keeps calling it normal.
solution.withBody: You know the day it moves. You have the number. You walk into the 3PL conversation with the evidence, not the feeling.
